analysis: All four units are documentation-only changes: docs/developer/test.md (head text 2731-3434 plus the changed range at about 2115-2131) and docs/operations/model-revisions.md (new 'Re-quantize and upload from CI' runbook section, about lines 171-296). No executable source, workflow YAML, or requant.py is supplied, so the described controls are unverified from this evidence. The runbook states: master-only ref guard, a secret-free preflight job, the prod environment with required-reviewer approval, hash-pinned tools, selftest before any secret, conditional immutable reservation, manifest uploaded last, byte-for-byte verification against a canonical manifest, and no register or promote step. These match the intent of A-004 and A-011 (model weights and artifact integrity), T-012 and T-027 (weight substitution), and the retained cache-routing tuple concern in T-041, whose aggregate comes from the manifest. The doc itself discloses residual risks: repository R2_* secrets are readable by any workflow a writer pushes; the prod deployment policy still allows v* branches and tags (ref guard only narrows the copy of the workflow it runs); and the legacy key set is the default. These are accurately documented and not new regressions from the docs. Integration questions for the next pass: whether .github/workflows/model-requant-upload.yml actually implements the documented gates (master-only, environment scoping, upload step holding only the chosen key set, the confirm_version requirement); whether manifest validation matches what Register and providers read; and whether public objects at models.darkbloom.ai are safe before registration. The test.md additions are descriptive test-coverage prose with no security-relevant behavior. The threat model may later need an entry for the CI model-upload pipeline and R2 credential custody, but that depends on the workflow source, which is not in this batch.
